account.password_policy: At least 10 characters, and not one that has appeared in a known breach.
account.password_change_signs_out: Changing your password signs out every other device and stops every API token you hold. This device stays signed in.
account.password_changed: Your password has been changed. Everywhere else has been signed out.
account.current_password_wrong: That is not your current password.
account.session_revoked: That device has been signed out.
account.session_gone: That device was already signed out.
account.no_sessions_hint: This is the only browser currently signed in to your account.

errors.UNAUTHENTICATED: This request needs a valid access token.
errors.FORBIDDEN: Your account is not permitted to do this.
errors.TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED: You are not a member of the company named in this request.
errors.TENANT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED: No active company could be determined for this request.
errors.TENANT_SUSPENDED: This company has been suspended by the platform.
errors.ACCOUNT_LOCKED: This account is locked. An administrator can unlock it.
errors.PASSWORD_POLICY_VIOLATION: The password does not meet the policy for this company.
errors.VALIDATION_ERROR: The request could not be accepted as sent.
errors.PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE: The request body is larger than this endpoint accepts.
errors.RATE_LIMITED: Too many requests. Retry after the period given in Retry-After.
errors.CONFLICT: The record is not in the state this request assumed.
errors.IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT: This idempotency key has already been used for a different request.
errors.INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION: That status change is not allowed from where this record is now.
errors.IMMUTABLE_RECORD: This record is posted and cannot be changed. Record a correction instead.
errors.DEPENDENT_RECORDS_EXIST: Other records point at this one, so it cannot be removed.
errors.INSUFFICIENT_STOCK: There is not enough of this part on hand.
errors.NEGATIVE_STOCK_NOT_ALLOWED: This would take the balance below zero, which this company does not allow.
errors.RESERVATION_EXPIRED: The reservation has expired and the stock has been released.
errors.METER_VALUE_DECREASED: A meter reading cannot be lower than the last one. Record a reset instead.
errors.CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE: Required checklist items are still unanswered.
errors.PARTS_NOT_RECONCILED: Issued parts must be consumed or returned before this can be closed.
errors.VERIFICATION_REQUIRED: This work still needs to be verified.
errors.APPROVAL_REQUIRED: This needs approval before it can go ahead.
errors.SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED: The person who raised this cannot approve it.
errors.CALENDAR_NOT_CONFIGURED: This factory has no working calendar, so the date cannot be worked out.
errors.SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED: The numbering sequence has no numbers left for this period.
errors.FILE_TOO_LARGE: The file is larger than the limit.
errors.UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE: That file type is not accepted here.
errors.FILE_SCAN_PENDING: The file is still being scanned. Try again shortly.
errors.SUBSCRIPTION_READ_ONLY: The subscription is in arrears, so this company is read-only. Reading and exporting still work.
errors.PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: This would go past what the current plan allows.
errors.DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE: A service this request depends on is unavailable. It is safe to retry.
errors.SERVER_ERROR: Something went wrong at our end. Quote the request id when reporting it.

api.idempotency_key_required: This endpoint requires an Idempotency-Key header.
api.idempotency_key_too_long: An Idempotency-Key may be at most 128 characters.
api.idempotency_body_changed: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.
api.idempotency_in_flight: The first request with this Idempotency-Key is still running.
api.token_company_mismatch: This token was issued for a different company. Request a token for the company you are naming.
api.client_cannot_switch_company: A machine client belongs to one company and cannot switch.
api.step_needs_a_person: This step is recorded against a person, so it cannot be taken by a machine client.
api.token_name_required: Give the token a name so it can be recognised later.
api.client_created: API client :name created. The secret is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.
api.secret_rotated: A new secret was issued for :name. The old one stops working immediately.
api.scope_unknown: A scope must be one of this company's own permission codes.
api.client_scope_denied: This client is not scoped for that operation.
api.api_clients_intro: Credentials for other software — an ERP posting costs, a dye house controller posting meter readings. Never issued to a person.
api.name: Name
api.scopes_required: Choose at least one scope. A client with none can do nothing.
api.scopes_hint: A credential is narrower than the person who created it. Tick only what this integration does; anything else is refused even if your own account could do it.
api.secret_shown_once: Copy the secret now. It is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.
api.secret_exchange_hint: Exchange these at POST /api/v1/auth/token for a bearer token.
api.expires_hint: Optional. Leave blank for no expiry.
api.revoke_confirm: Revoke this client? Anything using it stops working immediately.
api.no_clients_hint: Create one when another system needs to read or write here without a person signing in.

approval.workflows_intro: Who has to sign, and above what. Rules are ordered, and the order is the chain: a costly job goes to the factory manager and then to the owner, in that sequence.
approval.no_rules: No steps yet, so this chain asks nobody to sign.
approval.no_workflows_hint: Without one, work of any size starts without a signature.
approval.role_not_person_hint: A step names a role rather than a person, because a chain that names one person stops working the week they are on leave.
approval.rule_needs_a_condition: A step with no condition would match everything, and send a needle change to the company owner. Give it a cost, a criticality, or a factory.
approval.unknown_role: That role is not available to your company.
approval.remove_rule_confirm: Remove this step? Requests already raised keep the chain they were raised against.
approval.already_used: {1} :count request raised against it|[2,*] :count requests raised against it
approval.context_hint: Frozen when the request was raised. A later cost change never alters what an approver was shown.
approval.no_requests_hint: Work orders that need a signature appear here.
approval.not_pending: That request is no longer pending.
approval.no_current_step: That request has no step waiting on a decision.
approval.cannot_approve_own_request: You cannot approve a request you raised yourself. An approval you can grant yourself is a checkbox, not a control.
approval.not_your_step: This step is not waiting on you.
approval.rejection_needs_reason: A rejection needs a reason, otherwise the job is simply resubmitted unchanged.
approval.expired_automatically: Expired: nobody acted on it before the deadline.

asset.no_documents: No manual, diagram or certificate attached yet.
asset.document_delete_confirm: Remove this document? The file is deleted with it.
asset.no_documents_hint: The manual, the wiring diagram, the calibration certificate — anything a technician standing at this machine would need.
asset.locations_intro: Where machines stand. Everything above the factory is optional, so a flat list of line codes is a complete answer.
asset.location_hierarchy_hint: Fill in only the levels your factory actually models. Anything left blank simply drops out of the location path.
asset.location_delete_confirm: Remove :code? Only a location with no machines and no transfer history can be removed; close it instead.
asset.location_in_use: :count records name this location, so it cannot be removed. Close it instead, which keeps the history of where machines stood.
asset.location_factory_unavailable: That factory is not available to you.
asset.location_reference_unavailable: That selection is not available to your company.
asset.no_locations_hint: A machine has to stand somewhere: add a location before registering one, or import a list of them.
asset.delete_confirm: Remove :code? This is only for a machine registered by mistake — a machine that has been in service should be retired instead.
asset.delete_blocked_by_history: :count records are filed against this machine, so it cannot be removed. Retire it instead, which keeps its history.
asset.delete_blocked_by_children: This machine has sub-assets attached to it. Move or remove those first.
asset.page_description: Every machine on the floors you can reach.
asset.asset_code_readonly_hint: Printed on the machine — not changeable.
asset.factory_readonly_hint: Moving factories is a transfer, from the Transfers tab.
asset.name: Name
asset.depreciation_note: Depreciation is not included in these figures.
asset.nothing_posted_yet: Nothing posted against this machine yet.
asset.reversal_note: A correction is a reversal row, never an edit — the original stays exactly as posted.
asset.no_maintenance_history: No work orders recorded against this machine yet.
asset.search_placeholder: Asset code, name or serial number
asset.try_different_filter: Try a different search or filter.
asset.no_assets_hint: Adjust the filters, or register the first asset.
asset.no_transfers: This asset has never been transferred.
asset.reason_required_terminal: A reason is required for this status.
asset.request_transfer_hint: Move this machine to a different location or factory.
asset.qr_regenerated_desc: The old printed label will no longer scan.
asset.regenerate_qr_confirm_desc: The printed label stuck to the machine will stop scanning immediately — it must be reprinted and replaced.
asset.no_pending_transfers_hint: Transfers appear here while they await approval or receipt.
asset.transfer_received: Transfer :number completed. The asset has moved.
asset.version_conflict: This asset was changed by someone else while you were editing (they are on version :current, you submitted :submitted). Reload and reapply your change.
asset.category_type_mismatch: The selected category does not belong to the selected asset type.
asset.factory_change_needs_transfer: Move an asset between factories with a transfer, so the movement is recorded.
asset.currency_required_with_cost: A cost needs a currency; without one the figure has no meaning.
asset.parent_self: An asset cannot be its own parent.
asset.parent_cycle: That parent would create a loop in the asset hierarchy.
asset.parent_too_deep: The asset hierarchy is too deep to validate.

audit.no_entries_hint: Widen the dates, or clear the filters.
audit.append_only: Append-only. Entries are never edited or deleted; they are archived after two years and kept for seven.
audit.related: Everything else in the same request
audit.related_hint: One request often writes several rows. Seeing them together is usually the answer.

auth.failed: These credentials do not match our records.
auth.throttle: Too many login attempts. Please try again in :seconds seconds.
auth.account_inactive: This account is not active. Contact your administrator.
auth.account_locked: This account is temporarily locked after repeated failed attempts.
auth.tenant_access_denied: You do not have access to this company.
auth.no_company_membership: Your account is not linked to any company. Contact your administrator.
auth.tenant_context_required: No company context was established for this request.
auth.reset_link_sent: If that address belongs to an account, a reset link is on its way.
auth.password_reset: Your password has been reset. Sign in with the new one.

billing.no_contract_hint: Nothing is billed and nothing is restricted until a contract is recorded.
billing.read_only_banner: This subscription is read-only. Every screen, report and export still works; nothing new can be saved until the account is settled.
billing.read_only_message: The subscription is read-only, so this cannot be saved. Reports and exports still work, and settling the account restores writing.
billing.past_due_banner: An invoice is past its due date. Writing stops when the grace period ends.
billing.no_payments: Nothing received against this invoice yet
billing.usage_hint: Measured whether or not it is billed, so a renewal can be priced from what actually happened.
billing.transition_invalid: A subscription cannot go from :from to :to.
billing.invoice_immutable: An issued invoice cannot be changed. Correct it with a credit note, or void it and reissue.
billing.only_drafts_issue: Only a draft invoice can be issued.
billing.invoice_empty: An invoice with no value cannot be issued.
billing.no_priceable_lines: This contract is metered but none of its rates match a measured metric.
billing.invoice_not_payable: A :status invoice cannot take a payment.
billing.amount_positive: A payment must be for more than zero.
billing.amount_exceeds_balance: That is more than the outstanding balance of :balance. Record the balance, then issue a credit or a refund for the difference.
billing.already_reversed: That payment has already been reversed.
billing.credit_note_needs_issued: A draft invoice is corrected by editing it, not by a credit note.
billing.credit_note_amount: A credit note must be for more than zero and no more than the invoice total.
billing.cannot_void_paid: A paid invoice cannot be voided. Issue a credit note or a refund instead.
billing.limit_reached_active_factories: Your plan covers :limit factories, and they are all in use. Contact your provider to raise the limit.
billing.limit_reached_active_assets: Your plan covers :limit machines, and they are all in use. Retire a machine you no longer run, or contact your provider to raise the limit.
billing.limit_reached_active_users: Your plan covers :limit users, and they are all in use. Remove somebody who has left, or contact your provider to raise the limit.

breakdown.queued_offline: No connection. This report is saved on your device and will be sent as soon as the connection returns.
breakdown.failure_after_report: The machine cannot have stopped after it was reported.
breakdown.reported_in_future: A breakdown cannot be reported for a time that has not happened yet.
breakdown.timestamp_in_future: That time has not happened yet.
breakdown.timestamp_after_close: A closed breakdown's timeline cannot be edited.
breakdown.response_time_note: From report to technician arrival. Measured from the report, not the stoppage: time before anyone said so is a reporting problem, not a maintenance one.
breakdown.repair_time_note: Excludes hold time. Waiting for a part is a supply problem, not slow repair work.
breakdown.needs_review_note: An unclassified stoppage defaults to unplanned and is flagged, never silently dropped from availability.
breakdown.closure_needs_repair_completed_at: Record when the repair finished before closing.
breakdown.closure_needs_failure_code_id: A breakdown cannot be closed without a failure code.
breakdown.closure_needs_root_cause_id: A breakdown cannot be closed without a root cause.
breakdown.closure_reason_note: A breakdown closed with no recorded cause is a machine that broke for no reason. The failure reports are built from these two fields.
breakdown.recurrence_note: This machine already had an open breakdown, so this report is linked to it rather than counted as a second independent failure.
breakdown.invalid_transition: A breakdown cannot move from :from to :to.
breakdown.repair_never_started: Record when the repair started before completing it.
breakdown.cancel_needs_reason: Cancelling a breakdown needs a reason.
breakdown.start_work_order_description: Marks it in progress and moves this breakdown to IN_REPAIR.
breakdown.raise_work_order_description: Puts every technician on this line's roster onto a new work order for it — any of them can then open it and start.
breakdown.hold_time_note: Time on hold is tracked separately from repair time.
breakdown.close_description: A failure code and root cause are required — the failure-analysis reports are built from exactly these two fields.
breakdown.cancel_reason_hint: Why this report doesn't stand — a false alarm, a duplicate, or the machine turned out fine.
breakdown.asset_not_found: The selected machine does not exist.
breakdown.asset_terminal: A :status machine cannot have a breakdown reported against it.
breakdown.asset_outside_coverage: That machine is outside the line or department you cover.
breakdown.outside_coverage: This breakdown is outside the line or department you cover.
breakdown.problem_description_hint: Describe what the machine is doing. The failure code and root cause are filled in by maintenance later.
breakdown.photo_hint: Optional — a picture of the fault, if you have one. Saved with the report even offline.
breakdown.photo_error: Could not read that photo — try a different one, or skip it.
breakdown.failure_code_report_hint: Optional at report time — maintenance confirms or corrects it at closure.
breakdown.pick_machine_and_describe: Pick a machine and describe the problem before reporting.
breakdown.could_not_save_offline: Could not save this report on this device. Try again, or use a different browser mode.
breakdown.saved_and_sending: Saved on this device and sending now — check the sync icon if you're offline.
breakdown.impact_unit_note: Recorded in pieces. Converting output to money needs a costing rate this system does not hold.
breakdown.work_order_after_close: A closed breakdown cannot raise new work.
breakdown.work_order_already_open: Work order :number is still open — close or cancel it before raising another.
breakdown.no_maintenance_type: No maintenance type is configured, so repair work cannot be raised.
breakdown.page_description: Every machine stoppage on the floors you can reach.
breakdown.no_breakdowns_hint: Nothing is reported down right now.
breakdown.no_downtime_record: No downtime record yet — this breakdown hasn't reached a completed repair.

calendar.intro: When this factory is running. Availability divides downtime by scheduled operating time, and a maintenance date that falls on a rest day is moved to the next working one — both read what is set here.
calendar.no_factory_hint: Add a factory first; a calendar belongs to one.
calendar.no_weekly_off: Runs every day of the week.
calendar.not_set_yet: No working week set yet, so availability is being measured against a default one.
calendar.calendar_saved: The working week is in force.
calendar.must_start_later: A new working week has to start after :date, when the current one came into force. Two calendars claiming the same day cannot both be right.
calendar.invalid_weekday: A day of the week must be between Monday and Sunday.
calendar.factory_unavailable: That factory is not available to you.
calendar.end_shift_confirm: End :name from today? Past availability keeps reading against the hours it actually had.
calendar.no_shifts: No shifts yet. Without one, a scheduled operating time cannot be computed.
calendar.holiday_exists: That date is already on this factory calendar.

common.sync_will_send: Saved on this device. It will be sent as soon as the connection returns.
common.sending_now_check_sync: Sending now — check the sync icon if you're offline.
common.coming_soon: This module is not built yet.
common.reset_password_hint: We will email you a reset link
common.password_policy: At least 10 characters, and not a password known to have been breached.
common.confirm_delete: Remove this entry? This cannot be undone.
common.login_subtitle: Enter your credentials to access Annotech RMG.
common.login_highlight_maintenance: Preventive maintenance, scheduled and never missed
common.login_highlight_breakdown: Breakdowns reported and resolved from the factory floor
common.login_highlight_inventory: Spare parts and inventory under one roof
common.login_headline: Keep every machine running, and every record straight.
common.login_tagline: Maintenance, breakdowns, and asset lifecycle management built for RMG factory floors.
common.login_security_note: Every session encrypted, every company's data kept apart

cost.no_entries_hint: Labour and parts post themselves as work is recorded.
cost.derived_hint: Written by the system from the labour entries and part lines underneath, so a work order's cost cannot drift from its own records.
cost.derived_not_manual: Labour and parts costs are derived from the work order itself and cannot be posted by hand.
cost.amount_required: A cost entry needs an amount.
cost.category_missing: The :code cost category is missing, so this cost cannot be posted.
cost.already_reversed: That entry has already been reversed.
cost.cannot_reverse_a_reversal: A reversal cannot itself be reversed.
cost.reversal_hint: Append-only after posting. A correction is a reversal plus a new entry, never an edit.
cost.spend_against_value_hint: Maintenance spend as a share of what the machine cost. The figure that turns "this keeps breaking" into a decision.
cost.no_purchase_price: No purchase price recorded, so this cannot be calculated.
cost.depreciation_note: Accounting depreciation is deliberately excluded: it is a different question answered on a different basis (SRS 23).

dashboard.period_note: Every figure below covers this period and the factory selected in the header.
dashboard.overdue_hint: Past the grace period, not merely past the due date.
dashboard.availability_hint: Operating time as a share of scheduled operating time, against the factory shift calendar — not against 24 hours a day.
dashboard.mtbf_hint: Mean operating time between failures. Operating time, not calendar time.
dashboard.mttr_hint: Mean repair time, hold time excluded: waiting for a part is a supply problem, not slow repair work.
dashboard.mtta_hint: Report to acknowledgement. Measured from the report, because time before anyone said so is a reporting problem.
dashboard.failures_hint: Unplanned breakdowns. A duplicate report against a machine already down is not a second failure.
dashboard.cost_hint: Split because the two mean different things: one is the cost of keeping machines running, the other the cost of them stopping.
dashboard.unacknowledged_hint: A machine is down and nobody has picked it up yet.
dashboard.pm_compliance_hint: Preventive maintenance completed within its due date plus grace.
dashboard.low_stock_hint: At or below the reorder level. By the time stock is out, the lead time has already been lost.
dashboard.critical_low_hint: Parts whose absence stops a critical machine.
dashboard.trend_hint: Reported breakdowns against completed work orders, day by day for this period.
dashboard.no_technicians_on_duty: No active technicians on this factory.
dashboard.not_available_reason: Nothing happened in this period to compute it from. A zero would say something different.
dashboard.no_panels_hint: Your role has no dashboard panels. The lists in the sidebar are where your work is.

file.upload_failed: The file could not be uploaded. Try again.
file.type_not_allowed: Files of type :type are not accepted. Attach a photo (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC) or a PDF.
file.scan_pending: This file is still being checked. Try again in a moment.
file.infected: This file was rejected because a security check found a problem with it.
file.referenced_by_checklist: This file cannot be removed because a checklist result still points to it.

import.choose_file: Choose a CSV or Excel file
import.export_unavailable: This kind of data cannot be exported.
import.template_hint: The template contains the column names and one example row.
import.no_importers_hint: Importing appears here once you have permission to create the records it writes.
import.order_hint: Import in this order: locations first, then machines, then spare parts and history. A machine names its location by code, so the locations have to exist first.
import.no_recent: You have not imported anything yet
import.preview_hint: The first :count rows of your file, as they would be read.
import.confirm_hint: Rows with errors are skipped. Everything else is written.
import.not_confirmable: This import cannot be confirmed. It has either already run or has no valid rows.
import.not_cancellable: This import can no longer be cancelled.
import.queued: The import is running in the background.
import.not_permitted: You do not have permission to import this.
import.nothing_valid: No row in this file can be imported. Fix the errors and upload it again.
import.upload_failed: The file could not be uploaded.
import.too_many_rows: The file has more than :max rows. Split it and import in parts.
import.unsupported_file: Files of type :extension cannot be imported. Use CSV or XLSX.
import.type_not_allowed: A file of type :type cannot be imported.

errors.required: This column is required and was empty.
errors.unknown_reference: No record in this company has that code.
errors.date_format: Must be a date written as YYYY-MM-DD.
errors.datetime_format: Must be written as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.
errors.missing_columns: The file is missing required columns: :columns.
errors.duplicate_in_file: This code appears more than once in the file.
errors.category_type_mismatch: This category does not belong to the given asset type.
errors.location_factory_mismatch: This location belongs to a different factory.
errors.line_department_mismatch: This production line does not belong to the given department.
errors.started_after_completed: The start is later than the completion.
errors.not_in_the_past: This is history, so the date cannot be in the future.
errors.write_failed: The row passed checking but could not be written.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Where machines sit: line, station, department. Import these first.

assets.title: Machines
assets.description: The installed machine list, with type, location and purchase details.

spare_parts.title: Spare parts
spare_parts.description: The parts catalogue. Opening stock is received separately, through the store.

vendors.title: Vendors
vendors.description: Suppliers and service providers, from your purchasing list.

maintenance_history.title: Maintenance history
maintenance_history.description: Work already done, from whatever you were using before.

inventory.issue_return_intro: Consumables leaving the store without a work order: a box of gloves to the dye house, a roll of tape to the sewing floor.
inventory.issue_no_asset_warning: Nothing issued here is charged to a machine. Anything fitted to one should go through its work order instead, which is where the cost belongs and where the failure history can find it.
inventory.who_and_why: Who took it, and what for
inventory.no_direct_movements: Nothing issued outside a work order.
inventory.no_direct_movements_hint: Parts fitted to machines appear on their work orders instead.
inventory.no_compatibility: Nothing recorded. The store cannot tell what this part fits, or what will do instead.
inventory.substitutes_for: This part will do instead of
inventory.compatibility_already_listed: That model is already listed for this part.
inventory.cannot_substitute_itself: A part cannot stand in for itself.
inventory.unknown_asset_model: That model is not available to your company.
inventory.unknown_part: That part is not available to your company.
inventory.transfers_intro: Moving stock between factories. One factory asks, someone approves, the sending store dispatches, the receiving store confirms — and in between the stock is in neither, so a valuation taken while the van is on the road still balances.
inventory.awaiting_receipt: Waiting for the receiving factory to confirm.
inventory.request_a_part: Ask the store for a part
inventory.request_hint: This asks the store for the part. It moves no stock and reserves nothing — the store decides whether to issue it or order it.
inventory.cannot_cancel_issued: Parts have already been issued against this line, so the request cannot be withdrawn. Return what is not needed instead.
inventory.part_requests_intro: Every part asked for on an open job and not yet handed over, with what is on the shelf beside it. A stopped machine comes first, then the longest wait.
inventory.no_part_requests: Nothing is waiting on the store.
inventory.no_part_requests_hint: Requests made by technicians on open work orders appear here.
inventory.delete_confirm: Remove :number? Only a part nothing is filed against can be removed; one that has stock or history must be retired instead.
inventory.delete_blocked: :count records point at this part — stock movements, reservations or work order lines — so it cannot be removed. Retire it instead, which keeps the ledger readable.
inventory.deactivate_hint: A retired part disappears from every picker but keeps its stock ledger, so what was fitted to a machine two years ago still reads correctly. Parts are never deleted.
inventory.unknown_category: That category is not available to your company.
inventory.name: Name
inventory.no_parts_hint: Add the parts this factory keeps in store.
inventory.reorder_hint: Below the reorder level is the useful signal, not below zero. By the time stock is out, the lead time has already been lost.
inventory.threshold_note: Thresholds are policy. Quantities come from the ledger and are never typed in.
inventory.unit_cost_hint: Reference only. An issue is always costed at the weighted average in the ledger.
inventory.critical_hint: A part whose absence stops a critical machine.
inventory.available_hint: On hand minus what is already promised to somebody else's work order.
inventory.no_stock_hint: Receive stock into a bin to start the ledger.
inventory.ledger_hint: Append-only. A correction is a reversal row, never an edit, so the history shows both what was recorded and what was done about it.
inventory.already_reversed: That movement has already been reversed.
inventory.ledger_matches: {1} Ledger replays to the stored balance (1 movement).|[2,*] Ledger replays to the stored balance (:count movements).
inventory.ledger_mismatch: Ledger replays to :replayed but the balance says :balance. A movement was written outside the ledger.
inventory.quantity_must_be_positive: The quantity must be greater than zero.
inventory.insufficient_stock: Only :available of :part are available, and :requested were asked for.
inventory.adjustment_needs_reason: An adjustment needs a reason. Stock that moves without one is indistinguishable from loss.
inventory.reserve_after_close: A closed work order cannot reserve stock.
inventory.parts_after_close: A closed work order no longer accepts parts.
inventory.reservation_not_holding: That reservation is no longer holding stock.
inventory.release_exceeds_reservation: That is more than the reservation still holds.
inventory.issue_exceeds_reservation: That is more than the reservation still holds.
inventory.consume_exceeds_issued: Only :outstanding are still out of the store against this line.
inventory.return_exceeds_issued: Only :outstanding are still out of the store against this line.
inventory.negative_stock_allowed: This factory allows negative stock, so the issue was posted anyway.
inventory.outstanding_hint: Taken from the store but neither fitted nor returned. A work order cannot close while this is above zero.
inventory.substitute_hint: Recorded, because fitting a different part than the one specified is what a failure analysis needs to know later.
inventory.no_parts_on_work_order: No parts on this work order.
inventory.no_transfers_hint: Stock moving between factories appears here.
inventory.transfer_invalid_transition: A transfer cannot move from :from to :to.
inventory.transfer_needs_items: A transfer needs at least one part.
inventory.transfer_same_factory: A transfer needs two different factories.
inventory.transfer_needs_in_transit_bin: The source factory has no in-transit bin, so dispatched stock would have nowhere to sit.
inventory.in_transit_hint: Dispatched stock sits in an in-transit bin until it is received, so it is never in two places and never nowhere.
inventory.variance_hint: Dispatched but not received. A non-zero variance is a discrepancy to investigate, not something to write off.
inventory.receive_exceeds_dispatched: More cannot be received than was dispatched.
inventory.receive_needs_destination: Choose the bin the stock is going into.

maintenance.plan_has_occurrences: :count occurrences have been generated from this plan, so it cannot be removed. Deactivate it instead, which stops new ones and leaves the history explainable.
maintenance.template_intro: A checklist a technician is handed at the machine. Published versions are frozen — a revision is a new draft that takes effect when it is published.
maintenance.template_created: Checklist created. Add the checks it should carry.
maintenance.draft_started: A new draft is open. It takes effect when you publish it.
maintenance.publish_confirm: Publish this version? The one in force is archived, and every work order that ran it keeps resolving the version it actually used.
maintenance.version_published: Published. New work orders will be handed this version.
maintenance.version_is_frozen: This version is published and cannot be changed. Start a revision instead.
maintenance.platform_template_read_only: This checklist is supplied by the platform and shared with every company, so it cannot be edited.
maintenance.safety_hint: A safety check demands a photo and a note when it fails, and raises corrective work by itself. A tick in a box is not a record of a guard that was missing.
maintenance.name: Name
maintenance.label: Check
maintenance.seeded_hint: Provided with the system. Clone it to make changes.
maintenance.no_templates_hint: The system ships with templates for sewing, cutting, generators, boilers and compressors.
maintenance.no_items: This version has no items yet
maintenance.version_frozen: Version :version is published and cannot be edited. Create a new version instead, so historical work orders keep the checklist they were executed against.
maintenance.checklist_empty: A checklist needs at least one item.
maintenance.cannot_publish_empty: A checklist with no items cannot be published.
maintenance.needs_one_required_item: A checklist needs at least one required item. With none, a work order can be completed without a single answer.
maintenance.only_drafts_publish: Only a draft can be published; this version is :status.
maintenance.draft_already_open: Version :version is already an open draft. Finish or publish it first.
maintenance.item_type_unknown: Item :position has an unknown input type.
maintenance.tolerance_needs_numeric: Item :position sets a tolerance but is not a numeric check. The tolerance would be ignored at execution.
maintenance.tolerance_inverted: Item :position has a minimum above its maximum.
maintenance.choice_needs_options: Item :position is a choice but lists no options.
maintenance.non_working_day: If it falls on a non-working day
maintenance.no_plans_hint: A plan decides when a machine is serviced. Create one to start generating work.
maintenance.no_schedules_hint: Occurrences appear here once a plan is activated.
maintenance.preview_hint: A dry run. Nothing is saved until you submit.
maintenance.preview_needs_interval: Set an interval to see the dates.
maintenance.preview_rolling_note: A rolling plan has one occurrence outstanding at a time. This preview assumes each is completed exactly on its due date; in practice the next date shifts with the actual completion.
maintenance.plan_created: Plan :name created. Activate it when you are ready to generate work.
maintenance.plan_activated: Plan :name is active and generating occurrences.
maintenance.plan_deactivated: Plan :name deactivated. Existing occurrences are left in place.
maintenance.plan_needs_rules: A plan needs at least one trigger rule before it can be activated.
maintenance.plan_already_ended: This plan is past its end date.
maintenance.target_exactly_one: A plan applies either to one machine or to every machine of a type. Choose exactly one.
maintenance.interval_required: A calendar trigger needs an interval.
maintenance.meter_threshold_required: A meter trigger needs a meter and a threshold.
maintenance.rule_logic_required: Choose whether either condition triggers the work, or both are required. There is no sensible default: they are different maintenance regimes.
maintenance.template_must_be_published: Only a published checklist version can be attached. A draft could still change underneath the plan.
maintenance.skip_needs_reason: A skipped service is a compliance exception, so it needs a reason.
maintenance.schedule_completed: Marked complete. The next occurrence has been generated.

masterdata.intro: The reference lists the rest of the system is written in. The platform supplies a starter set for the garment industry; anything your company adds is your own.
masterdata.import_hint: These lists can also be filled from a spreadsheet. Import writes the same rows this screen does, so use whichever suits the number of them.
masterdata.empty_hint: Add the first entry with the form beside this list, or import a spreadsheet of them.
masterdata.delete_confirm: Remove this entry? Only an entry nothing is filed against can be removed; anything in use must be deactivated instead.
masterdata.copied_hint: Copied from a platform entry. Give it a code of its own — two entries cannot share one.
masterdata.platform_row_read_only: This entry is supplied by the platform and shared with every company, so it cannot be edited. Add your own entry instead.
masterdata.code_taken: That code is already in use in this list.
masterdata.unknown_reference: That selection is not available to your company.
masterdata.in_use: This entry is used by :count records and cannot be removed. Deactivate it instead so it stops appearing in new work.

descriptions.buildings: The buildings on a factory site.
descriptions.departments: Sewing, knitting, dyeing, finishing, utility — how the factory is organised.
descriptions.sections: A narrower grouping inside a department.
descriptions.production-lines: The line a machine stands on, which is how a floor supervisor names it.
descriptions.workstations: A single station on a line.
descriptions.asset-types: The kind of machine: sewing, cutting, finishing, utility.
descriptions.asset-categories: A narrower grouping inside a type.
descriptions.failure-categories: The broad kind of fault: mechanical, electrical, operator.
descriptions.failure-codes: The specific fault, under its category.
descriptions.root-causes: What was found to be behind the fault.
descriptions.downtime-reason-codes: Why a machine was stopped, and whether that stoppage counts against availability.
descriptions.maintenance-types: Preventive, predictive, corrective — and whether each is planned work.
descriptions.meter-types: What is counted on a machine: running hours, stitches, cycles.
descriptions.warehouses: A store building on a factory site.
descriptions.stores: A store room inside a warehouse.
descriptions.bins: The shelf a part actually sits on. Every stock movement names one, so a company cannot receive a part until a bin exists.
descriptions.cost-categories: What a cost was for, and which lifecycle bucket it rolls into.

metering.none_on_this_machine: No meter is fitted to this machine, so a usage-based plan has nothing to measure.
metering.intro: What is counted on each machine. A plan can say "service every 500 running hours", and until somebody records the hours it can never come due.
metering.stale: Not read for over a fortnight
metering.no_meters_hint: Fit a meter to a machine from its own screen. Usage-based maintenance has nothing to hang off until one exists.
metering.no_meters_on_asset_hint: Attach one from the Metering screen to start tracking readings here.
metering.reading_triggered: {1} Reading recorded, and it brought one maintenance job due.|[2,*] Reading recorded, and it brought :count maintenance jobs due.
metering.reading_in_future: A reading cannot be taken in the future.
metering.value_decreased: This meter reads :current and cannot go down to :submitted. If the meter was replaced, record that instead so the drop has an explanation.
metering.unknown_meter_type: That meter type is not available to your company.
metering.already_fitted: This machine already has a :type meter. Two of the same kind would give every usage-based due date two answers.

notification.escalations_intro: How long something may sit unanswered before it goes past the person who ignored it. Level 1 is the first nudge; each level after it reaches further up.
notification.stop_on_acknowledge: Stop once somebody picks it up
notification.no_rules_hint: Without one, an alert nobody reads is an alert nobody ever hears about again.
notification.remove_rule_confirm: Remove this rule? Alerts already sent are unaffected.
notification.unknown_role: That role is not available to your company.
notification.factory_unavailable: That factory is not available to you.
notification.level_already_covered: Level :level is already covered for this event. Two rules at one level would tell the same person twice about one silence.
notification.role_not_person_hint: A rule names a role rather than a person, because one that names an individual stops working the week they are away — which is exactly the week somebody needs it.
notification.acknowledge_hint: Acknowledging stops the escalation. Opening the list does not: reading is not the same as picking something up.
notification.no_notifications_hint: Breakdowns, overdue maintenance and approvals arrive here.
notification.in_app_always_on: Always on. The record of what happened is part of the audit trail, not a preference.
notification.channels_hint: These decide how loudly you are told. Everything still appears in this list.
notification.not_yet_delivered_hint: Email, SMS and WhatsApp delivery land with the messaging workstream. The preference is recorded now so nothing has to be reconfigured later.

MAINTENANCE_OVERDUE.title: Maintenance overdue: :asset
MAINTENANCE_OVERDUE.body: :plan was due on :due_at and is past its grace period.

WARRANTY_EXPIRY.title: Warranty ending: :asset
WARRANTY_EXPIRY.body: Cover from :vendor ends on :end_date, in :days days.

WEBHOOK_DISABLED.title: Webhook disabled: :url
WEBHOOK_DISABLED.body: It failed :count times in a row and has been switched off. Fix the receiver, then enable it again.

SUPPORT_ACCESS.title: Support access to your data
SUPPORT_ACCESS.body: :name from support was given access to :company until :until. Reason given: :reason

TICKET_RESOLVED.title: Ticket marked resolved: :subject
TICKET_RESOLVED.body: If this did not fix it, reply and it reopens automatically.

numbering.intro: What this company's work orders, breakdowns and transfers are called.
numbering.reset_confirm: Go back to the platform default (:format)? It takes effect from the next period.
numbering.already_issued: {1} :count number already issued|[2,*] :count numbers already issued
numbering.next_period_notice: A change here renumbers nothing. Numbers already issued keep the shape they were given, and the new format takes effect when the counter next restarts — at the start of the next month or year.
numbering.gaps_note: Gaps in a run of numbers are normal. A number is allocated before the record is saved and is never reused, so a cancelled document leaves its number behind rather than passing it on.
numbering.saved: :type numbering saved. It takes effect from the next period.
numbering.reset_done: :type numbering is back to the platform default.
numbering.format_length: A format must be between 1 and 128 characters.
numbering.format_characters: A format may contain letters, digits, hyphens, slashes and full stops besides the placeholders.
numbering.sequence_required: The format must contain {SEQ}. Without the counter, every document in the period would be given the same number.
numbering.factory_required: This counter runs separately in each factory, so the format must contain {FACTORY}. Without it two factories would issue the same number on the same day.
numbering.month_required: This counter restarts each month, so the format must contain {MM} and {YYYY}. Without the month, January's first number and February's would be the same string.
numbering.month_not_allowed: This counter restarts once a year, so {MM} would put a month in the number that the counter does not follow.

platform.tenants_intro: Every company on this installation, their contracts and their size.
platform.no_data_access_note: Counts and contracts only. Seeing a customer's machines, work orders or breakdowns requires an audited support grant, and the customer is told when one is opened.
platform.company_code_hint: Appears inside every work order and breakdown number this customer will ever issue. Short, and hard to change afterwards.
platform.no_tenants_hint: Create the first one to get started.
platform.new_tenant_intro: Creates the company, its first factory and its owner account together. All three are needed before anybody can sign in and do anything.
platform.first_factory_hint: Machines live in a factory, document numbers are issued per factory, and the working calendar hangs off it. A company without one cannot be used. More can be added by the customer.
platform.owner_hint: The first person who can sign in. They get the Company Owner role, company-wide, and can invite everybody else.
platform.owner_credentials_once: Give these to the customer now. The password is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.
platform.code_taken: That code is already in use, including by a deleted company.
platform.owner_email_taken: An account with this email already exists. Adding an existing person to a new company is a different operation — do it from the company's own user screen after a support grant.
platform.no_contract_yet: No contract has been recorded for this customer yet.
platform.new_contract_hint: Saving supersedes the current contract rather than editing it: an invoice already raised under the old terms has been sent to somebody, and changing what it was calculated from makes it unexplainable.
platform.contract_saved: Contract saved. The previous one has been archived.
platform.auto_renew: Renew automatically at the end of the term
platform.suspend_confirm: Suspend this customer? Everybody is signed out and nobody can sign in until it is reversed. No data is deleted.
platform.suspended: :name has been suspended. Their data is untouched.
platform.support_access_hint: Seeing a customer's data requires a reason, expires by itself, and is announced to the customer. You then act as one of their users, which means you see exactly what that person sees and no more.
platform.reason_example: Ticket 4471: work orders not appearing after a factory transfer.
platform.reason_too_short: Write a real reason. It goes to the customer and into the audit log.
platform.support_opened: Access opened. The customer has been notified.
platform.no_grants: Nobody has been given access to this customer.
platform.grant_not_active: That access has ended or expired. Open a new one.
platform.not_a_member: That person is not an active member of this company.
platform.support_session_banner: Support session — you are inside a customer's account
platform.growth_chart_label: New customers by month, the last six months
platform.limits_are_advisory: Recorded for billing. Nothing is blocked when a customer goes over.
platform.limits_are_enforced: Enforced. At the limit, adding another factory, machine or user is refused. Anything already over the limit is left alone — only the next one is stopped.
platform.supersedes_notice: Saving this archives :number. Invoices already raised under it are left alone.
platform.act_as_hint: Whoever you pick is named in the audit log. Acting as the owner and acting as a storekeeper are different amounts of access.
platform.currently_suspended: This company is suspended. Nobody in it can sign in.
platform.suspend_hint: Stops everybody in this company from signing in. Nothing is deleted, and reactivating restores access immediately.
platform.suspension_reason_hint: Shown to the customer word for word on the screen that tells them they are stopped.
platform.suspension_reason_example: Invoice INV-2026-0042 unpaid since 30 June, after three reminders.
platform.no_invoices_hint: Raise one below, or let the scheduled run issue the first on the billing cycle.
platform.invoice_drafted: Invoice :number drafted. Check it, then issue it.
platform.no_contract_to_invoice: This customer has no contract, so there is nothing to invoice against. Record a contract first.
platform.code_is_fixed: The code :code cannot be changed. It is inside every work order and breakdown number this customer has issued.
platform.reset_hint: Signs the account out everywhere and stops its API tokens. The new password is shown once, here.
platform.reset_confirm: Issue a new password for :name? They are signed out everywhere immediately.
platform.reset_shown_once: Give this to the customer now. It is shown once and cannot be retrieved again.
platform.password_reset_done: A new password has been issued for :name.
platform.reset_reason_example: Owner locked out; company email account closed. Ticket 5120.
platform.credential_change_notice: The :what for :account was changed by support. Reason: :reason
platform.customer_login_hint: The owner account — the one the customer signs in with, and the only one nobody inside their company can reset. Both changes are announced to the customer and recorded in the audit log.
platform.customer_id_hint: This is what they type to sign in. Change it when the address was mistyped or the mailbox is gone.
platform.limits_hint: What this customer is allowed. Changing these does not change their contract, its price or its term.
platform.limits_blank_hint: Leave a box empty for no limit.
platform.limits_need_contract: Limits live on the contract, so this customer needs one before limits can be set.
platform.overage_effect: Only Block actually stops anything: at the limit, adding another is refused. Warn only and Allow and bill let the work carry on and settle it commercially.
platform.domain_none: This customer uses the shared address. Add one below to give them their own.
platform.domain_host_hint: For a subdomain, type only the first part — it is added to :base. For their own domain, type the whole address.
platform.domain_remove_confirm: Remove :host? Anybody using it will have to go back to the shared address.
platform.domain_added: :host has been added. It will not work until the records below are in place.
platform.domain_primary_set: :host is now the address this customer is given.
platform.domain_taken: That address is already in use by a customer.
platform.domain_invalid: That does not look like a web address.
platform.domain_verify_first: An address has to be working before it can be the primary one.
platform.domain_not_found_yet: The record is not visible yet. DNS changes can take a few hours to spread — try again later.
platform.domain_verify_first_note: Until this is done the address does not reach anybody, which is deliberate: honouring an unproven claim would let one customer collect another's sign-ins.
platform.domain_steps: What the customer has to do
platform.domain_step_cname: Add a CNAME record pointing their address at ours:
platform.domain_step_txt: Add a TXT record proving they own it:
platform.domain_step_check: Then press Check now. DNS changes can take a few hours to spread.
platform.domain_tls_note: A new address also needs an HTTPS certificate on the server. That is done by the server, not from this screen — see docs/11-Deployment.md.
platform.support_desk_intro: Who is inside a customer's data, and who has been.
platform.support_none_open: Nobody has access to a customer's data.
platform.support_no_history: No support access has been opened
platform.support_no_history_hint: Every grant ever opened is listed here, with who opened it and why.
platform.notifications_intro: What the rest of the platform staff have done.
platform.notifications_empty_hint: Support access, suspensions and closures appear here as they happen.
platform.notify_erased: :name erased :company and all of its data
platform.close_hint: Ends the account. Everybody in this company is signed out and cannot sign in again, and the customer disappears from the list above.
platform.close_reversible: Nothing is deleted. A closed account can be reopened, and everything in it comes back exactly as it was.
platform.confirm_code_label: Type the customer code :code to confirm
platform.confirm_code_mismatch: That is not the customer code. Type :code exactly.
platform.closed_done: :name has been closed. It can still be reopened from the list.
platform.closed_customers_hint: Closed accounts keep all their data and can be reopened. Erasing one is permanent.
platform.erase_hint: Deletes this customer and everything in it — machines, work orders, breakdowns, stock, invoices and users' access. This cannot be undone.
platform.erase_no_export: There is no tenant export yet, so nothing is kept. If the customer may ever ask for their records back, reopen the account instead.
platform.erase_audit_kept: The audit log survives: what was done, by whom and when is kept even after the data it describes is gone.
platform.erased_done: :name and all of its data have been erased.
platform.finance_intro: What each customer has paid, what is still owed, and what running the platform costs.
platform.refunded_note: Includes :amount :currency refunded, already taken off the received figure.
platform.no_money_by_month: Nothing has been received or spent in the last twelve months.
platform.no_money_yet_hint: Once a customer has a contract and an invoice, the totals appear here.
platform.no_billed_customers_hint: Give a customer a contract, then raise their first invoice from their Billing tab.
platform.nothing_overdue_hint: Every issued invoice is either paid or still inside its due date.
platform.no_payments_hint: Each payment recorded against an invoice appears here, newest first.
platform.expense_remove_confirm: Remove this cost from the totals?
platform.no_expenses_hint: Hosting, domains, software and the rest. Without them the net figure is only income.
platform.edit_company_hint: The customer's own details. Their code is fixed and cannot be changed here.
platform.logo_hint: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 512 KB. Shown at 120×120.
platform.no_usage_history: No usage has been measured yet. The first month appears after billing:advance next runs.
platform.tickets_intro: Ask the provider something, in writing.
platform.tickets_desk_intro: Every customer's tickets, in one inbox.
platform.ticket_opened: Ticket opened. The provider has been told.
platform.ticket_closed: This ticket is closed. Open a new one to raise it again.
platform.ticket_status_invalid: That is not a valid status.
platform.no_tickets_hint: This customer has not raised anything with the provider.
platform.no_tickets_hint_tenant: When something needs the provider's attention, raise it here.
platform.tickets_no_closed_hint: Every ticket, once it is answered and closed, is listed here.

report.no_reports_hint: Reports appear here once you have permission to the data behind them.
report.no_rows: Nothing to show for this period and scope
report.not_permitted: You do not have permission to export this report.
report.unknown_format: That export format is not available.
report.ready: Your report is ready to download.
report.queued: Your report is being generated. It will appear here when it is ready.
report.will_queue: This report is large, so it will be generated in the background.
report.preview_note: Showing the first :count rows. Export to get every row.
report.scoped_by_header: Scoped to the factory selected in the header.

job.none: You have not generated any reports yet
job.none_hint: Run a report and export it; the file will appear here.
job.retention: Generated files are kept for :days days.

asset_register.description: Every machine on the books, with what it is and where it is.

asset_status.title: Asset status history
asset_status.description: How machine status changed over a period, and why.

asset_transfer.title: Asset transfers
asset_transfer.description: Machines moved between factories and locations, including those still in transit.

maintenance_history.title: Maintenance history
maintenance_history.description: What was done to a machine, when, and what it cost.

pm_compliance.title: PM compliance
pm_compliance.description: Preventive maintenance completed within its grace period, per machine.

overdue_maintenance.title: Overdue maintenance
overdue_maintenance.description: What is late right now, past its grace period.

breakdown_analysis.title: Breakdown analysis
breakdown_analysis.description: Every stoppage with its full timestamp chain.

root_cause.title: Root cause analysis
root_cause.description: Failures grouped by cause and failure code, with the downtime each caused.

downtime.title: Downtime

reliability.title: MTBF and MTTR
reliability.description: Reliability per machine: failures, mean time between them, and mean repair time.

maintenance_cost.title: Maintenance cost
maintenance_cost.description: Posted cost entries with their currency, rate and base amount.

lifecycle_cost.title: Lifecycle cost
lifecycle_cost.description: What each machine has cost since it arrived.

parts_consumption.title: Parts consumption
parts_consumption.description: Which spare parts were consumed, in what quantity and at what value.

inventory_valuation.title: Inventory valuation
inventory_valuation.description: Current stock on hand at weighted average cost.

technician_performance.title: Technician workload
technician_performance.description: Jobs assigned and completed, and labour hours booked.

vendor_performance.title: Vendor performance
vendor_performance.description: Claims filed against each vendor, how many they honoured, and how long they took.

coverage_expiry.title: Warranty and AMC expiry
coverage_expiry.description: Cover running out, soonest first, with what it will cost to keep.

scan.not_found_title: This code doesn't match any machine you can reach
scan.not_found_hint: It may belong to a different company, or the label may be damaged. Ask your supervisor if this seems wrong.
scan.location_not_found_title: This code doesn't match any location you can reach
scan.location_not_found_hint: It may belong to a different company, or the label may be damaged. Ask your supervisor if this seems wrong.
scan.what_would_you_like_to_do: What would you like to do?
scan.no_actions: You have no actions available on this asset.
scan.no_assets_here: Nothing is recorded at this location
scan.no_assets_here_hint: Either the location is empty, or an asset here has not been registered yet.
scan.label_hint: Print on adhesive stock. Minimum 20 mm square when printed; smaller will not scan reliably from an oily machine frame.
scan.label_truncated: Showing the first 200 labels. Narrow the filter to print the rest.
scan.no_labels_hint: Register an asset first, or widen the filter.
scan.regenerate_qr_confirm: This invalidates the label currently stuck to the machine. It must be reprinted and replaced. Continue?
scan.qr_regenerated: A new QR token was issued (:code). Reprint and replace the label on the machine.

settings.intro: How this company wants the product to behave. Several of these change what a number means rather than how a screen looks — whether planned downtime counts against availability, what a maintenance date does when it lands on a rest day — so every change here is recorded in the audit log.
settings.scope_hint: Some settings can be answered again for a single factory. A factory that has not answered follows the company, and keeps following it when the company changes its mind.
settings.reset_to_company: This factory follows the company again.
settings.factories_intro: The units everything else is scoped to. A machine, a work order and a shift all belong to one.
settings.code_hint: Up to five letters or digits. It goes on every label and work order number.
settings.code_is_permanent: Set once. Changing it would strand labels and work order numbers already issued.
settings.timezone_hint: Downtime, response times and shift boundaries are all measured on this clock.
settings.factory_delete_confirm: Remove :name? Only a factory with no machines in it can be removed; one that has run should be closed instead.
settings.factory_in_use: :count machines are registered in this factory, so it cannot be removed. Close it instead — it still owns everything that ever happened in it.
settings.no_factories_hint: Add the first one before registering machines: every machine, work order and shift belongs to a factory.

team.intro: Who a job goes to when it does not go to one person: the night shift electricians, the dye house crew. Work orders, breakdowns, plans, approval steps and escalation rules can all name a team.
team.name: Team name
team.delete_confirm: Remove :name? Only a team nothing was ever handed to can be removed.
team.in_use: :count records were handed to this team, so it cannot be removed. Take it out of use instead — a job still has to be able to say who it went to.
team.factory_unavailable: That factory is not available to you.
team.no_teams_hint: Without one, every job has to be handed to a named person.

technician.skills_hint: Separate from the area they cover: a dyeing technician may hold an electrical certificate, and the person to send to a tripped panel at 2am is the one who has it.
technician.skill_example: Soft flow dyeing, VFD, boiler operation
technician.skill_already_listed: That skill is already listed for this person.
technician.intro: Who is on the floor and what they look after. A dyeing technician covers the dye house, a sewing mechanic the sewing floor.
technician.name: Name
technician.login_hint: Optional. A technician may work without a login, and a supervisor records the work for them.
technician.search: Search by name or employee ID
technician.covers_hint: This decides who the assignment screen offers first. It never decides who may be assigned — at two in the morning a manager sends whoever is awake.
technician.specialization_example: Dyeing machines, boiler and generator, sewing machines
technician.workload_hint: The most open work orders this person may hold at once. Leave blank for no limit.
technician.delete_confirm: Remove :name? Only somebody with no work behind them can be removed; take them off the roster instead.
technician.in_use: :count records name this person — assignments and time entries — so they cannot be removed. Take them off the roster instead, which keeps every repair they worked on readable.
technician.factory_unavailable: That factory is not available to you.
technician.area_unavailable: That selection is not available to your company.
technician.line_needs_department: A production line needs its department named too, otherwise the roster has nothing to widen to when that line is quiet.
technician.login_already_linked: That login is already :name's — one account cannot be shared between technicians, since it would make their work history unrecoverable.
technician.no_technicians_hint: Add the people who do the work. Without them a work order can be raised but not assigned.

tenancy.suspended_lede: Your company's access has been stopped by the provider. Nobody in your company can sign in until it is restored.
tenancy.suspended_data_safe: Nothing has been deleted. Every machine, work order, breakdown and stock record is exactly where you left it, and will be there when access is restored.
tenancy.suspended_what_now: Contact your provider to have this reviewed. If it concerns an unpaid invoice, settling it is usually enough.
tenancy.closed_body: This company's account has been closed and can no longer be used.
tenancy.closed_what_now: If you believe this is a mistake, contact your provider. An account can be reopened for a short while after it is closed.

user.users_intro: Who works in this company and what they may do. An account can belong to more than one company in a group; this screen manages its place in this one.
user.name: Name
user.email_is_the_account: The address identifies the account across every company it belongs to, so it is not changed here.
user.factory_hint: Used by the factory-scoped roles below. A company role covers every factory whatever is chosen here.
user.coverage_hint: Only used by a role like Line Chief, which reports breakdowns without a technician record of its own — restricts which machines they may report a breakdown against.
user.roles_intro: What each role can do. Worth reading before handing one out.
user.roles_read_only: Seeded roles are shared by every company and cannot be edited. Cloning one to make your own is not built yet.
user.removed: :name no longer has access to this company.
user.password_reset: A new password has been issued for :name.
user.password_will_be_generated: A password will be generated and shown once when this person is added. Most people on a factory floor have no working email address, so it is handed over rather than emailed.
user.password_shown_once: Password for :email — shown once, and not readable again.
user.password_hint: Write it down or hand it over now. Reset it from this screen if it is lost.
user.reset_confirm: Issue a new password for :name? Their current one stops working immediately.
user.remove_confirm: Remove :name from this company? Their account and everything they signed off stay exactly where they are.
user.already_a_member: That person is already a member of this company.
user.roles_required: Choose at least one role. A member with no role can sign in and do nothing.
user.factory_required: A factory-scoped role needs a factory, otherwise it grants nothing anywhere.
user.cannot_remove_yourself: You cannot remove your own access.
user.cannot_suspend_yourself: You cannot suspend your own access.
user.last_administrator: This is the last person who can manage users. Give somebody else that ability first, or the company would have no way back in.
user.no_users_hint: Add the people who will use the system: technicians record work, managers approve it.

vendor.archived: Vendor archived. Existing records still name them.
vendor.archive_confirm: Archive this vendor? Past costs, warranties and contracts keep naming them.
vendor.no_vendors_hint: Add the suppliers you buy parts from and the companies that service your machines.
vendor.name: Name
vendor.blacklisted_hint: Blacklisted vendors cannot be chosen for new work. Existing records are untouched.
vendor.no_warranties_hint: Recording cover is what lets a technician be told a repair is already paid for.
vendor.exclusions_hint: Worth writing down: "covered" and "covered except consumables" are different answers to the question a technician is asking.
vendor.incident_date_hint: The date the machine failed decides whether cover applied, not today.
vendor.contract_renewed: Contract renewed. The previous one is kept as it was agreed.
vendor.no_contracts_hint: An AMC recorded here is what stops a covered machine being repaired at your own cost.
vendor.scope_hint: Choose one machine, a factory, or tick the machines it covers. A contract with no scope covers nothing.
vendor.renew_hint: Renewing creates a new contract and keeps this one as it was agreed. Editing dates here would erase what was signed.
vendor.end_before_start: The end date is before the start date.
vendor.not_a_service_vendor: That vendor is a parts supplier, not a service provider.
vendor.contract_scope_required: Choose what this contract covers: a machine, a factory, or a list of machines.
vendor.not_covered_on: The warranty was not in force on :date.
vendor.claim_description_required: Say what happened. A claim without it cannot be answered by the vendor.
vendor.claim_transition_invalid: A claim cannot go from :from to :to.
vendor.rejection_reason_required: Record why the vendor rejected it.
vendor.settled_amount_required: Record how much was actually settled.
vendor.cannot_renew_cancelled: A cancelled contract cannot be renewed.
vendor.cancel_reason_required: Say why the contract is being cancelled.

webhook.no_endpoints_hint: Add one to send breakdowns, work orders and stock movements to another system as they happen.
webhook.rotated: A new signing secret has been issued. The previous one keeps working for 24 hours.
webhook.paused: Endpoint paused. Nothing will be sent until it is enabled again.
webhook.secret_shown_once: Copy this signing secret now. It is never shown again.
webhook.secret_hint: Sign requests with HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a full stop, and the exact request body. Compare against the :header header.
webhook.rotation_hint: During a rotation, both signatures are sent for 24 hours so a receiver can switch over on its own schedule.
webhook.no_deliveries: Nothing sent to this endpoint yet
webhook.url_invalid: That is not a URL this system can call.
webhook.url_https_required: Webhook URLs must use HTTPS. A signed payload over plain HTTP can be read by anyone on the path.
webhook.url_no_credentials: Do not put a username or password in the URL. Use the signing secret instead.
webhook.url_private: That address is on a private or reserved network, so this system will not call it.
webhook.events_required: Choose at least one event. An endpoint subscribed to nothing never sends anything.
webhook.endpoint_not_deliverable: The endpoint is paused or disabled.

work_order.covers_this_area: Looks after this part of the floor
work_order.invalid_transition: A work order cannot move from :from to :to.
work_order.assign_needs_technician: Assign at least one technician first.
work_order.checklist_incomplete: :count required checklist items are still unanswered.
work_order.verification_not_required: This work order does not require verification.
work_order.cannot_verify_own_work: Verification needs a second pair of eyes: you cannot verify work you completed yourself.
work_order.verification_required: This work order must be verified before it can be closed.
work_order.approval_pending: This work order is still awaiting approval.
work_order.cancel_needs_reason: Cancelling a work order needs a reason.
work_order.reopen_needs_reason: Reopening a completed work order needs a reason.
work_order.asset_not_found: The selected machine does not exist.
work_order.asset_terminal: A :status machine cannot have new work raised against it.
work_order.schedule_not_open: This maintenance occurrence is no longer open.
work_order.labor_after_close: A closed work order no longer accepts labour entries.
work_order.labor_end_before_start: The end time must be after the start time.
work_order.labor_in_future: Labour cannot be recorded for a time that has not happened yet.
work_order.labor_too_long: A single labour entry cannot exceed 24 hours. Split it across shifts.
work_order.labor_needs_technician: Choose the technician who did the work.
work_order.labor_overlap: This technician already has time recorded from :from to :to. One person cannot be in two places at once.
work_order.checklist_needs_in_progress: A checklist can only be answered while the work is in progress.
work_order.checklist_required_not_na: A required item cannot be marked not applicable.
work_order.checklist_no_version: This work order has no checklist attached.
work_order.checklist_item_not_on_version: That item does not belong to this work order's checklist.
work_order.checklist_reading_not_numeric: The reading must be a number.
work_order.checklist_choice_invalid: Choose one of the listed options for :item (:options).
work_order.checklist_fail_needs_note: A failure on ":item" needs a note describing what was found.
work_order.checklist_fail_needs_photo: A failure on ":item" needs a photo as evidence.
work_order.checklist_file_not_found: That attachment does not belong to this work order.
work_order.followup_description:
Raised automatically by a failed check on work order :number.

Item: :item
Observation: :observation
work_order.assign_after_close: A closed work order cannot be reassigned.
work_order.technician_not_found: One of the selected technicians does not exist.
work_order.technician_other_factory: :name works at another factory. Sending them here is a transfer, not an assignment.
work_order.not_assigned: That technician is not on this work order.
work_order.repair_time_note: Excludes hold time: waiting for a part is a supply problem, not slow repair work.
work_order.no_attachments_hint: Photos of the finished job, a vendor's note, anything worth keeping with this record.
work_order.parts_pending_note: Parts cost lands with the inventory module.
work_order.verified_by_other: Verification needs someone other than the person who did the work.
work_order.page_description: Every scheduled and in-progress job on the floors you can reach.
work_order.no_work_orders_hint: Raise one from here, or let an active maintenance plan generate it.
work_order.my_work_page_hint: Your own queue — in-progress first, then by priority.
work_order.no_my_work_hint: Work assigned to you appears here.
work_order.not_a_technician: Your account is not linked to a technician record, so it has no work queue.
work_order.no_parts: No parts on this work order yet.
work_order.request_a_part_hint: Asks for it — only the store can hand one over.
work_order.issue_a_part_hint: The store handing one over directly, with nothing requested first.
work_order.checklist_version_hint: The version is frozen onto the work order now, so a template edited later does not change what this technician was asked to check.
work_order.shutdown_hint: The machine stops for this job, and its stoppage counts as planned downtime.
work_order.parts_outstanding: This work order still holds parts on :count line(s) that were neither fitted nor returned. Account for them before closing.
work_order.approval_rejected: This work order was rejected at approval and cannot be started.
